  The keeping of a light is not dramatic work.
  Most nights nothing happens. The lamp
  turns. The clockwork hums. Ships pass at a
  distance and never know her name. Sometimes
  a fishing boat comes close enough that she
  can see the faces of the men on deck, and
  she raises a hand, and sometimes they raise
  one back.

  In October a storm came in from the
  southwest with no warning the radio had
  caught. The wind hit the tower like a fist.
